standard_prerequisites.name: Localization square for a morphism of topoi
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the commutative square of topoi and the functor behaviour that the ringed statement refines; also underlies the identification (f')^{-1}j_V^{-1} = j_U^{-1}f^{-1} used in the composite.

standard_prerequisites.name: j^{-1} = j^* on sheaves of modules for a localization morphism
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Stacks Project, Modules on Sites, discussion of localization morphisms
standard_prerequisites.use: Used in the author's closing remark to pass from the first functor equality to the second.

core_obligations: Construct (f')^\sharp as the composite (f')^{-1}\mathcal{O}'_V = (f')^{-1}j_V^{-1}\mathcal{O}' = j_U^{-1}f^{-1}\mathcal{O}' \xrightarrow{j_U^{-1}f^\sharp} j_U^{-1}\mathcal{O} = \mathcal{O}_U (proof lines 2615-2621).
Take the remaining conclusions of the ringed square from Sites, Lemma sites-lemma-localize-morphism applied to the underlying morphism of topoi (proof lines 2622-2623).
Note that j^{-1} = j^* on sheaves of modules when j is a localization morphism, so the equality f'_*j_U^{-1} = j_V^{-1}f_* implies f'_*j_U^* = j_V^*f_* (proof lines 2624-2625).
proof_roadmap: Define the sheaf-of-rings map (f')^\sharp by the displayed composite.
Inherit the commutative square and functor equalities from the unringed Sites lemma.
Bridge the j^{-1} and j^* versions of the pushforward equality via the localization remark.
difficulty_reason: The proof is a construction: it defines the map of sheaves of rings (f')^\sharp by the displayed composite (f')^{-1}\mathcal{O}'_V = (f')^{-1}j_V^{-1}\mathcal{O}' = j_U^{-1}f^{-1}\mathcal{O}' \xrightarrow{j_U^{-1}f^\sharp} j_U^{-1}\mathcal{O} = \mathcal{O}_U, which is exactly the new datum the statement asks for; the remaining conclusions (commutativity of the ringed square and the functor equalities) are then taken from the unringed localization lemma of Sites applied to the underlying morphism of topoi, with the final remark that j^{-1} = j^* on sheaves of modules for a localization morphism so the first functor equality implies the second. The explicit composite and the bridging remark are the substance.
